title: Dead or Alive 4
subtitle: A tournament enters another console generation

body: Dead or Alive 4 is Team Ninja's Xbox 360 fighting game, released in Japan and North America on 29 December 2005. Helena Douglas attempts to confront corruption within DOATEC while the series' ninjas continue their struggle against the organisation. The story introduces new competitors before making them available elsewhere, connecting a familiar tournament structure to the expanding cast. The new console gives the fighters and arenas a more detailed presentation. Underneath it remains a quick contest of strikes, throws and defensive responses, where recognising an opponent's intention can matter as much as completing a combination.

The exchange between attacking, throwing and countering encourages the player to vary a pattern that has become predictable. Movement within the arena offers another way to alter the distance or approach, while the surroundings can carry an encounter beyond its initial position. A fighter's familiar actions have to work against a person who may now be expecting them. Learning therefore involves more than memorising a move list. It means noticing which responses the opponent favours and choosing an action that makes that habit less useful in the next exchange.

Online features gave the new console's players a way to continue those contests beyond the living room. Tomonobu Itagaki directed alongside Katsunori Ehara and Hiroaki Matsui, with the game becoming his final Dead or Alive fighting release before leaving Tecmo. Reviews were generally favourable, and sales passed one million copies during 2006. Later backward compatibility brought it to Xbox One and Xbox Series systems. Its original place remains close to the Xbox 360's arrival, presenting a recognised fighting series as a demonstration of the new machine's character and online possibilities.
